channel.title: The Valley Times-News - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Valley Times-News (valleytimes-news.com)

item.title: CONTRIBUTOR'S VIEW - Lynn Gendusa: When Pride Picks Up a Chainsaw
item.description: Lynn Gendusa recalls wielding a chainsaw on a rainy hillside and failing as a church secretary to show how pride, stubborn roots, and faith can keep us from asking for help.

item.title: CONTRIBUTOR'S VIEW - Cathy Hunt: Delivering a One-Two Punch
item.description: A viral baby monkey named Punch melts hearts worldwide—but Cathy Hunt asks whether we show the same compassion for struggling people close to home, especially 'the least of these.'

item.title: FLM organizes community Easter egg hunt
item.description: FLM Alumni Inc. hosts a Family and Friends Community Easter Egg Hunt March 28 at Fantasy Field in LaFayette.

item.title: Alabama Lions Sight talks eye care efforts for those in need
item.description: Alabama Lions Sight has improved vision for more than 500,000 residents since 1944, offering screenings, exams and low-cost eye care to Alabamians who otherwise couldn’t afford it.

item.title: Local leaders network with LaFayette students
item.description: LaFayette teens will meet local leaders, hear career stories, and network over food and games at Youth Leadership Night on March 11 at The Spot on the Square.

item.title: LaFayette expresses interest in neighborhood watch
item.description: LaFayette councilmember Charlene Story is working with police to restart the city’s neighborhood watch, focusing on community ties and prevention, with a March 24 planning meeting.

item.title: CONTRIBUTOR'S VIEW - Dean Collins: Blessing Follows Obedience
item.description: Dean Collins links daily writing discipline to Christian discipleship, urging believers to move from comfortable learning to obedient action, where blessing follows.

item.title: CONTRIBUTOR'S VIEW - Bill King: What It Was, Was Soccer
item.description: Bill King recalls Andy Griffith's "What It Was, Was Football" as he learns the game of soccer from the sidelines, watching his grandson play at Glenwood High.

item.title: Beulah Family Day returns next month
item.description: Beulah Family Day returns April 18 with games, live music, a $1 car smash and a Top 20 Car Show at Beulah Elementary School; admission is free, with low-cost food and activities.

item.title: Community center explores aquatic family seating options
item.description: Valley Parks and Rec plans picnic tables at the pool, funded by local business donations and an April 12 crawfish boil; tickets on sale March 9–April 3 at the community center.
